clue.text: Wretched grave provided by heartless Udall

indicators.note: a thing without its heart has lost its middle, so the central letters of the name go

blocks.note: a pit is a hole dug for burial
'provided' and 'if' both introduce a condition
the name with its middle letters DAL removed

explanation.surface: Some poor soul called Udall ends up in a miserable grave.
explanation.walkthrough: PIT + IF + UL, the outer letters of Udall.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitiful and wretched are synonyms, both describing a state that arouses pity.

clue.text: Colours aren't vulgar in the outskirts of Paris

indicators.note: this word only marks the slang form; the actual insertion is signalled by 'in'
the outskirts of a place are its edges, so only the outer letters are used

blocks.note: ain't is the nonstandard, colloquial form of aren't
first and last letters of Paris

explanation.surface: In the Paris suburbs, colours are never garish.
explanation.walkthrough: P(AINT)S: the slang 'ain't' sits between the outer letters of Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: To paint something is to colour it, so the verbs paints and colours are synonyms.

clue.text: Art managed to entertain setter with six details of little importance

indicators.note: something managed is handled and arranged, so these letters are put in a new order
to entertain guests is to take them in, so the outer piece holds the rest

blocks.note: the three letters rearranged
the setter refers to themselves as I
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: An art curator hosts the setter, armed with half a dozen minor points.
explanation.walkthrough: TR(I + VI)A.
explanation.definitionFit: Trivia are unimportant facts or details, from the Latin for crossroads, a place of idle talk.

clue.text: One Green surprisingly seen in showy vehicle

indicators.note: a surprising result is an unexpected arrangement, so these letters are rearranged
things seen in a place are inside it, so these letters go within the next word

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
the five letters rearranged
fine can mean elaborate or ornate

explanation.surface: A Green politician is unexpectedly spotted in a flashy car.
explanation.walkthrough: F(I + REENG)INE. A Green may be a member of the Green Party, which makes the showy vehicle a surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire engine is a vehicle that carries firefighters and their equipment.

clue.text: Two short men standing up to drink

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing up means reading upward, so the letters go from bottom to top

blocks.note: Reg and Al, short forms of Reginald and Alan or Albert

explanation.surface: Two small men stand up and have a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: REG + AL read upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Lager is a type of light beer, an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Deputy adopting unusual word for a bit of morning moisture

indicators.note: something unusual is out of its normal order, so these letters are rearranged
to adopt is to take in, so the first piece takes the other inside it

blocks.note: DEP is a standard abbreviation for deputy
the four letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A deputy picks an odd term to describe the morning dew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deputy' here takes its three-letter abbreviation, and the jumbled word goes between its second and third letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A dewdrop is a single droplet of condensation that forms on grass and leaves overnight.

clue.text: Lie Isolde spun to keep things moving on track?

definitions.text: to keep things moving on track?

indicators.note: spun means twisted around, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Isolde tells a spun-out lie to keep her story on track.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'on track' means on a railway, not on schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: Diesel oil fuels diesel locomotives, so it keeps trains running on railway lines.

clue.text: Decline of Rooney announced

indicators.note: something announced is spoken out, so the answer is what the name sounds like

blocks.note: Wayne Rooney is a famous England footballer

explanation.surface: The decline of a footballer is announced.
explanation.walkthrough: Wayne Rooney, the England and Manchester United striker; the first name is pronounced the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To wane is to decrease or diminish, like the moon after it is full.

clue.text: Backlash after establishment leader is moved down three places

indicators.text: leader is moved down three places
indicators.note: the leader is the opening letter, and shifting it three positions along changes the word's order

blocks.note: a creation is something established or founded

explanation.surface: A backlash follows when the head of an organisation is demoted.
explanation.walkthrough: The leader of CREATION is its C; move it three letters later and you get the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A backlash is a strong adverse reaction to something.

clue.text: Expecting man and older relative in port

indicators.note: in says the man and relative sit inside the abbreviation

blocks.note: PT is the abbreviation for port
Reg is a man's name
nan is a grandmother

explanation.surface: Expecting a man and his grandmother to arrive in the harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: P(REG + NAN)T.
explanation.definitionFit: Expecting is an idiom for carrying an unborn child.

clue.text: More distant chemical supplier once to monarch

blocks.note: Imperial Chemical Industries, a former British chemicals giant
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword queen

explanation.surface: A former chemicals firm supplies the sovereign.
explanation.walkthrough: ICI was a major British chemical company, broken up in the 2000s, hence 'once'.
explanation.definitionFit: Icier can mean cooler or more aloof in manner, so a more distant person is icier.

clue.text: Good to get back into fruit?

blocks.note: G is the usual abbreviation for good
to re-engage is to take part again or reconnect

explanation.surface: Is getting back into fruit a good idea?
explanation.walkthrough: G + REENGAGE; 'get back into' looks like a container signal but is a definition of its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A greengage is a kind of small green plum.

clue.text: Initially, old European litter is recycled to make soap, shampoo etc.

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the next word only
recycled material is broken down and made into something new, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: first letter of old
E is the abbreviation for European
taken as written

explanation.surface: Waste is recycled into bathroom products.
explanation.walkthrough: O and E join the letters of litter is to make the ten letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Toiletries are items used for washing and grooming, of which soap and shampoo are examples.

clue.text: Knock out some Beatles tunes

indicators.note: 'some' means only part of the following words is used

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: Some Beatles songs are knockouts.
explanation.walkthrough: beatleS TUNes.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun is to knock someone senseless with a blow.

clue.text: Self-restraint of sailors with ten nice brews

indicators.note: brewing mixes ingredients together, so these letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: ABs are able seamen
the seven letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Sailors show restraint with ten good beers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brews' reads as a noun for drinks but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstinence is refraining from indulgence, especially alcohol, which is a form of self-control.

clue.text: Road taken by fool and brother to confess to PM?

indicators.note: something taken by another is held by it, so the first piece goes inside the second

blocks.note: RD is the abbreviation for road
a goon is a silly person
BR is the abbreviation for brother
to own up is to confess

explanation.surface: A man taken along by a fool and his brother is asked to confess to the Prime Minister.
explanation.walkthrough: GO(RD)ON + BR + OWN. Gordon Brown was UK Prime Minister 2007-10.
explanation.definitionFit: Gordon Brown served as Britain's Prime Minister, so the abbreviation PM names him by example.

clue.text: Coach in support of discipline

indicators.note: in says the coach sits inside the support

blocks.note: a rest is a support, as in an armrest
to coach is to train

explanation.surface: A sports coach backs a disciplined approach.
explanation.walkthrough: RES(TRAIN)T.
explanation.definitionFit: Restraint is self-control, the ability to hold back, which discipline also means.

clue.text: Wandering bear dancing at rave

indicators.note: dancing feet move around, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the four letters rearranged
to rave is to talk wildly, to rant

explanation.surface: A bear wanders in and starts dancing at a rave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rave' looks like a party but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberrant means straying from the normal course, from the Latin for wandering away.

clue.text: Danes upset about mermaid's third letter to storyteller

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so these letters are tipped into a new order
third points to the letter in third position of the word it follows
about means around, so the jumbled letters surround the selected one

blocks.note: the five letters rearranged
the third letter of mermaid
an en is a printer's measure, and the spelt-out name of the letter N

explanation.surface: Upset Danes write about The Little Mermaid to its author.
explanation.walkthrough: ANDE(R)S + EN. The Little Mermaid is one of the tales of the Danish author, so the surface stays in his world.
explanation.definitionFit: Hans Christian Andersen was a Danish writer famous for fairy tales, so he is a storyteller.

clue.text: Bishop eating pineapple set fire to dessert

indicators.note: something eating food takes it inside, so the bishop's letters surround the fruit

blocks.note: Bp is a standard abbreviation for bishop
ananas is the French and botanical name for the pineapple
lit is the past tense of light, to set fire to

explanation.surface: A bishop eats pineapple, then flambés his pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: Bishop is usually B in chess, which leaves a stray P; here it is the church abbreviation Bp, split around the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A banana split is a dessert of a halved banana with ice cream and toppings.

clue.text: Comes up with popular heir

blocks.note: a hit is a popular success
a son is traditionally the heir

explanation.surface: A popular heir thinks of something.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit on an idea is to discover it, an idiom equivalent to coming up with it.

clue.text: Look into crash in winter race

indicators.note: into means going inside, so the first piece is placed in the second

blocks.note: to slam is to crash or bang
lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: Investigate a crash during a winter ski race.
explanation.walkthrough: SL(LO)AM; 'Look into' reads as 'investigate'.
explanation.definitionFit: A slalom is a downhill ski race around a zigzag course of gates.

clue.text: Animals retreating into grass

indicators.note: a retreating army goes backwards, so the word is read from end to start

blocks.note: deer are animals

explanation.surface: Animals withdraw into long grass.
explanation.definitionFit: A reed is a tall grass-like plant growing in wet ground.

clue.text: Wise puritan translated Latin

indicators.note: translating turns text into another form, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: a prude is a person shocked by impropriety
the five letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A sensible puritan translated some Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puritan' looks like anagram fodder beside 'translated', but it gives PRUDE; only Latin is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Prudential means showing prudence, careful good judgment, so it is a synonym of wise.

clue.text: Prepare doctor's letter

blocks.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor
ess is the spelt-out name of the letter S

explanation.surface: Get ready the letter from the GP.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor's letter' looks like a sick note; DR + ESS.
explanation.definitionFit: To dress food is to prepare it, for example cleaning a chicken or seasoning a salad.

clue.text: Native American's short statement of belief

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: a creed is a formal statement of beliefs

explanation.surface: A Native American gives a short statement of belief.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cree are a Native American people of Canada and the northern United States.

clue.text: Self-confident, so be of use carrying note

indicators.note: carrying something means holding it, so the note goes inside

blocks.note: as and so both mean 'therefore' or 'because'
to serve is to be useful
ti is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A confident musician makes himself useful by carrying a note.
explanation.walkthrough: AS + SER(TI)VE.
explanation.definitionFit: Assertive describes someone who states their views boldly, showing self-assurance.

clue.text: Sound of "M" in China's alphabet?

indicators.note: 'in' says the answer sits inside the following words

blocks.note: the letters span the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: Is there an M sound in the Chinese alphabet?
explanation.walkthrough: chiNA'S ALphabet. Chinese uses characters not an alphabet, which is why the clue ends with a question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: M is a nasal consonant: it is voiced with air passing through the nose.

clue.text: Beat man to function

blocks.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them
gent is short for gentleman

explanation.surface: Someone is hit on the way to a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangent is one of the trigonometric functions, alongside sine and cosine.

clue.text: Doctor turns me into bone!

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A patient complains that a physician is turning him to bone.
explanation.definitionFit: The sternum is the breastbone, the flat bone at the front of the chest.
